correctness.rationale: The differential map is bijective and the last difference bit selects exactly one lift from a residue modulo n to a given residue modulo 2n. Direct output comparison proves the exact burst-ball local formula. Fourier inversion is exact. For proper nontrivial Fourier orders d dividing n/2, cyclic rotation cancellation proves zero transfer-matrix trace and determinant -(1-z²)^d; Cayley–Hamilton gives the claimed scalar transfer power. Primitive n-th modes cancel by reversal and complement. Inversion yields every coefficient. Independently enumerating distinct deletion outputs at n=4,8,16 and exact integer difference-DP through n=64 agrees. No appeal to unproved computational extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The closest full primary works establish binary DVT two-burst correction/covering (arXiv:2606.15379v1) and cardinality generating functions (Babu et al. 2025), but their results do not determine the full distribution of distinct two-burst descendants among codewords of each fixed syndrome class. The two-class all-power-of-two polynomial law refines both known scalar constraints. Searches for the exact invariant, equivalent transition-statistic Fourier transforms, and more general covering literature produced no implication covering this assertion. Possible unindexed/implicit transfer-matrix coverage remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: A previously unindexed or implicitly equivalent two-state/cyclotomic transfer-matrix identity could give the same generating polynomials.

value.rationale: The 2026 perfect-code theorem invites analysis of how its equal total coverage is distributed across individual codewords. The exact coefficient law classifies every possible burst-output multiplicity, separates four exceptional from 2n−4 regular syndrome classes, and identifies the precise singleton-ball boundary. This is a natural infinite-family complete distribution, not an arbitrary numerical slice. It does not assert rate gains or decoding-speed improvements.
